sql_injection.title: SQL Injection
steps: Replace all dynamic SQL string concatenation with parameterized queries or prepared statements
Apply strict input validation using allowlists — reject unexpected characters (quotes, semicolons, dashes)
Adopt an ORM (SQLAlchemy, Hibernate, ActiveRecord) that handles escaping by default
Apply the principle of least privilege: database accounts used by the application should have only SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on required tables, never DROP or EXECUTE
Enable a Web Application Firewall rule set targeting SQL injection payloads as a defense-in-depth measure
Review stored procedures for dynamic SQL construction and convert them to parameterized variants
Enable database activity monitoring and alerting for anomalous query patterns
Conduct a code review of all database interaction layers using SAST tooling (Semgrep, CodeQL)

code_examples.python_sqlalchemy:
# WRONG
db.execute(f'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}')
# CORRECT
db.execute(text('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = :id'), {'id': user_id})
code_examples.python_raw:
# WRONG
cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = \'' + name + '\'')
# CORRECT
cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s', (name,))

cross_site_scripting.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
steps: Apply context-sensitive output encoding for all user-supplied data rendered in HTML (HTML encode), JavaScript (JS encode), CSS (CSS encode), and URL (URL encode) contexts
Use a modern frontend framework (React, Vue, Angular) that auto-escapes output by default — avoid dangerouslySetInnerHTML / v-html / [innerHTML] unless absolutely necessary
Implement a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) header: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'
Set the HttpOnly flag on session cookies to prevent JavaScript access
Apply input validation to reject unexpected HTML tags and JavaScript event handlers in user input
Use DOMPurify or similar library to sanitize any rich text that must allow HTML
Enable X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block header for legacy browsers
Conduct SAST scanning to identify all reflection points where user input is rendered

code_examples.csp_header:
# Nginx CSP header
add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self';" always;

ssrf.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
steps: Validate and sanitize all URLs provided by users before making server-side HTTP requests
Implement an allowlist of permitted external hostnames/IP ranges — deny all others by default
Resolve hostnames server-side and validate the resulting IP address against the allowlist (DNS rebinding protection)
Use a dedicated HTTP client library configured to disallow redirects to private addresses
Disable unnecessary URL-fetching features (XML external entity processing, PDF renderers that fetch external resources)
Run outbound HTTP requests through an egress proxy that enforces the allowlist at the network layer
Monitor and alert on outbound HTTP requests to internal network ranges

path_traversal.title: Path Traversal / Directory Traversal
steps: Never construct file paths directly from user input — use a fixed base directory and map user input to filenames within it
Normalize and canonicalize all file paths using os.path.realpath() or Path.resolve() before use
Verify the resolved path starts with the expected base directory (jail check)
Maintain an allowlist of permitted file extensions and filenames
Remove or encode path separator characters (/, \, ..) from all user input
Run the application process with minimal filesystem permissions using OS-level sandboxing
Disable directory listing on web servers (Options -Indexes in Apache, autoindex off in Nginx)

code_examples.python:
import os
BASE_DIR = '/var/app/uploads'
# WRONG
path = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, user_filename)
# CORRECT
path = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(BASE_DIR, user_filename))
if not path.startswith(BASE_DIR + os.sep):
    raise ValueError('Invalid path')

auth_bypass.title: Authentication Bypass
steps: Enforce authentication checks on every protected endpoint at the framework/middleware level rather than individual handlers
Implement a centralized authentication middleware that runs before all routes
Use a framework-level authorization decorator or guard (not ad-hoc per-function checks)
Test each endpoint independently for missing authentication — use an unauthenticated HTTP client
Ensure API versioning changes don't bypass authentication middleware (e.g., /api/v2/ endpoint missing auth guards)
Implement proper HTTP method enforcement (GET vs POST) and reject unexpected methods
Validate JWT signature and expiry on every request, reject tokens signed with 'none' algorithm
Implement rate limiting on authentication endpoints to prevent brute force

code_examples.fastapi:
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException
from app.core.auth import get_current_user

# WRONG — auth only applied to some endpoints
@router.get('/admin/users')
async def get_users():
    return users  # Missing auth!

# CORRECT — auth applied via dependency
@router.get('/admin/users')
async def get_users(current_user = Depends(get_current_user)):
    return users

exposed_admin_panel.title: Exposed Admin Panel
steps: Move admin interfaces to a non-standard URL path not guessable by automated scanners
Restrict access to admin panels by IP allowlist at the network/WAF layer
Require multi-factor authentication for all administrative access
Implement a separate authentication domain or VPN requirement for admin access
Remove or disable default admin credentials immediately after deployment
Apply HTTP Basic Authentication as an additional layer before the admin application itself
Monitor and alert on failed authentication attempts to admin endpoints
Regularly audit admin user accounts and remove unused accounts

missing_security_headers.title: Missing or Misconfigured Security Headers
steps: Add Content-Security-Policy header with a strict policy that disallows inline scripts and unsafe-eval
Set Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload to enforce HTTPS
Add X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN to prevent clickjacking
Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff to prevent MIME type sniffing
Add Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin to control referrer leakage
Set Permissions-Policy to disable unused browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation)
Configure CORS headers to explicitly allowlist permitted origins — never use Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
Use SecurityHeaders.com to validate headers after implementation

code_examples.fastapi:
from fastapi.middleware.trustedhost import TrustedHostMiddleware
from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware

class SecurityHeadersMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):
        response = await call_next(request)
        response.headers['X-Content-Type-Options'] = 'nosniff'
        response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = 'DENY'
        response.headers['Referrer-Policy'] = 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin'
        return response

weak_tls.title: Weak TLS Configuration
steps: Disable TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 — support only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3
Configure a strong cipher suite order: prefer ECDHE key exchange and AES-GCM/CHACHA20 ciphers
Disable weak ciphers: RC4, DES, 3DES, MD5-signed certificates, NULL ciphers, export ciphers
Enable OCSP stapling to improve certificate validation performance and privacy
Implement HSTS with a minimum max-age of 1 year and includeSubDomains
Submit your domain to the HSTS preload list at hstspreload.org
Use a minimum RSA key size of 2048 bits or ECDSA P-256
Renew certificates at least 30 days before expiry — use Let's Encrypt with auto-renewal

code_examples.openssl_test:
# Test TLS configuration
openssl s_client -connect yourdomain.com:443 -tls1   # Should fail
openssl s_client -connect yourdomain.com:443 -tls1_1 # Should fail
openssl s_client -connect yourdomain.com:443 -tls1_2 # Should succeed
# Also use: https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/

jwt_vulnerabilities.title: JWT Vulnerabilities (Algorithm Confusion, Weak Secret)
steps: Explicitly specify and validate the expected algorithm in JWT verification — never trust the 'alg' header from the token
Reject tokens with alg: 'none' — configure your library to require a specific signing algorithm
Use strong, random secrets for HMAC: minimum 256 bits (32 random bytes) — generate with: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"
For production, prefer RS256 or ES256 (asymmetric keys) over HS256 to separate signing from verification
Set appropriate expiry (exp claim): access tokens 15–30 minutes, refresh tokens 7–30 days
Validate all standard claims: exp, nbf, iss, aud
Implement token revocation for sensitive operations using a token blacklist or jti (JWT ID) tracking
Rotate signing keys periodically and support key versioning via kid (key ID) header

code_examples.python_pyjwt:
import jwt

# WRONG: trusts the algorithm from the token header
payload = jwt.decode(token, secret, algorithms=None)  # Never do this!

# CORRECT: explicitly specify allowed algorithms
payload = jwt.decode(
    token,
    secret,
    algorithms=['HS256'],  # Only allow HS256
    options={'require': ['exp', 'iss', 'aud']},
    audience='legioncyber-shield',
    issuer='api.shield.legioncyber.com'
)

cors_misconfiguration.title: CORS Misconfiguration
steps: Define an explicit allowlist of trusted origins — never use Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
Do not reflect the Origin header value back without validation
If using wildcard origin, ensure Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is NOT set to true (this combination is forbidden by browsers but some frameworks allow it incorrectly)
Restrict allowed methods to only those required (GET, POST) — avoid exposing PUT/DELETE via CORS to third-party origins
Set a narrow Access-Control-Allow-Headers list
Set the Vary: Origin response header when dynamic origin allowlisting is used
Test CORS configuration with both an allowlisted and non-allowlisted origin using curl

code_examples.fastapi:
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=['https://shield.legioncyber.com'],  # Explicit allowlist, NOT '*'
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE', 'OPTIONS'],
    allow_headers=['Authorization', 'Content-Type'],
)

exposed_secrets.title: Exposed Secrets / Credentials in Responses or Source
steps: Immediately rotate any exposed credentials, API keys, tokens, or passwords
Remove secrets from all code repositories — use git filter-repo or BFG Repo Cleaner to purge git history
Move all secrets to environment variables or a dedicated secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault)
Add .env, *.pem, *.key, credentials.json to .gitignore
Implement pre-commit hooks with Gitleaks or truffleHog to prevent future secret commits
Enable GitHub/GitLab secret scanning alerts
Audit API responses for accidentally included secret fields and strip them in serializers
Implement secrets rotation policy (30–90 days for API keys)

code_examples.python_env:
# WRONG: hardcoded secret
AWS_SECRET = 'AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE'

# CORRECT: from environment
import os
AWS_SECRET = os.environ['AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY']
# Or with python-decouple / pydantic BaseSettings:
from app.config import settings
aws_secret = settings.aws_secret_access_key
code_examples.gitleaks:
# Install and run Gitleaks
brew install gitleaks
gitleaks detect --source . --verbose

# Add as pre-commit hook
# .pre-commit-config.yaml:
- repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
  rev: v8.18.0
  hooks:
    - id: gitleaks

insecure_deserialization.title: Insecure Deserialization
steps: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources using native language deserialization mechanisms (Python pickle, Java ObjectInputStream, PHP unserialize)
Use data-only serialization formats: JSON, Protocol Buffers, MessagePack, or Avro instead of language-native formats
If native deserialization is unavoidable, implement integrity checks (HMAC signature) before deserialization
Apply allowlist deserialization — only allow expected classes/types to be deserialized
Run deserialization in a sandboxed environment with minimal permissions
Monitor for deserialization gadget chain indicators in application logs
Update libraries with known deserialization vulnerabilities (Jackson, XStream, SnakeYAML)

code_examples.python_wrong:
# WRONG: pickle can execute arbitrary code
import pickle
obj = pickle.loads(request.body)  # Never do this with untrusted data!

# CORRECT: use JSON or another safe format
import json
obj = json.loads(request.body)  # Safe — no code execution

xxe.title: XML External Entity Injection (XXE)
steps: Disable external entity processing in all XML parsers — this is typically OFF by default only in newer library versions
Disable DOCTYPE declarations if not required
Use a modern, secure XML library with safe defaults (defusedxml in Python)
Where possible, use JSON instead of XML for data exchange
Validate XML input against a strict schema (XSD) before processing
Update XML libraries to latest versions which often disable XXE by default

code_examples.python:
# WRONG: standard ElementTree may be vulnerable in older Python versions
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
tree = ET.parse(user_xml_file)  # May be vulnerable

# CORRECT: use defusedxml
import defusedxml.ElementTree as ET
tree = ET.parse(user_xml_file)  # Safe

command_injection.title: Command Injection / OS Command Injection
steps: Avoid using shell=True in subprocess calls — always use argument lists to prevent shell interpretation
Never construct OS commands by concatenating user input
Use language-native library functions instead of shell commands where possible (e.g., os.rename() instead of shell 'mv')
Apply strict input validation with allowlists before passing any input near shell commands
Use shlex.quote() (Python) or ProcessBuilder (Java) for unavoidable dynamic arguments
Run the application process with minimal OS privileges — apply principle of least privilege
Implement Linux seccomp filters to restrict system calls available to the process
Monitor for unusual child process spawning in application telemetry

code_examples.python:
import subprocess

# WRONG: shell=True allows injection
subprocess.run(f'convert {user_filename} output.pdf', shell=True)

# CORRECT: argument list, no shell
subprocess.run(['convert', user_filename, 'output.pdf'], check=True)

# Also validate the filename first:
import re
if not re.match(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$', user_filename):
    raise ValueError('Invalid filename')

directory_listing.title: Directory Listing Enabled
steps: Disable directory listing in web server configuration
Ensure all directories accessible via the web contain an index file
Review which directories are exposed via web server configuration and remove unnecessary ones
Apply access controls to any directory that must be accessible but should not be browsable
Audit web root for sensitive files that may be exposed (backups, configuration files, .git directories)

code_examples.nginx:
# Disable directory listing in Nginx (default is off, but confirm explicitly)
autoindex off;

default_credentials.title: Default Credentials
steps: Immediately change all default credentials on all services, databases, admin panels, and network devices
Implement a first-run wizard that forces credential change before system is usable
Audit all third-party components and SaaS integrations for default credentials
Implement account lockout after 5–10 failed login attempts
Enable MFA on all administrative interfaces
Use a password manager and enforce strong password policies (minimum 16 characters, complexity requirements)
Maintain an inventory of all services with admin interfaces and review credentials quarterly
Remove or disable demo/test accounts in production deployments

code_examples.check_script:
#!/bin/bash
# Check for common default credentials
services=('redis:6379' 'postgres:5432' 'elasticsearch:9200' 'kibana:5601')
for svc in "${services[@]}"; do
  host="${svc%:*}"
  port="${svc#*:}"
  echo "Checking $host:$port for open access..."
  nc -z -w2 $host $port && echo "WARNING: $svc is reachable!" || echo "OK: $svc not reachable"
done
